intent: The link whose hover or keyboard focus opens its HoverCard's preview.
typical_uses: A link to a person, a document or another record that the card previews

dont_use_when.situation: A link with no preview attached to it

instead.target: a plain `<a>` element or the app router's link component
instead.note: The kit ships no standalone link component; a link that previews nothing needs no HoverCard around it.

dont_use_when.situation: An icon-only button whose label should appear on hover

invariants.text: Hovering opens the card for mouse pointers only, after `delay` milliseconds (600 when not given); keyboard focus that shows a focus ring opens it after the same delay. A card opened by hover closes `closeDelay` milliseconds (300 when not given) after the pointer leaves both the trigger and the card.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `href`, or a link element through `render`; an `<a>` without `href` is not a link, takes no keyboard focus and so never opens the card for keyboard users

a11y.by: the primitive's PreviewCard.Trigger renders a native <a>; hover-card.test.tsx asserts the trigger is found by its link role and accessible name and that its tagName is 'A'

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's PreviewCard.createHandle(), tying this trigger to a HoverCard root it is not placed inside
handle.because: `PreviewCardHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the card's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

payload.states: payload is any value handed to the root's function children when this trigger opens the card
payload.because: Typed by the caller's own `Payload` type parameter (`unknown` here), so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; hover-card.module.css styles no trigger, so the link keeps the look the caller gives it.

good.title: A handle linking to a profile
The app router's link rendered as the trigger, opening sooner
good.code:
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCardTrigger delay={300} render={<RouterLink to="/docs/spec" />}>
    Specification
  </HoverCardTrigger>
  <HoverCardContent>The current draft of the specification.</HoverCardContent>
</HoverCard>

bad.title: A kit Button nested inside the trigger
bad.why: The trigger already renders an `<a>`, so this nests a button inside a link, which HTML does not allow; put the caption straight into the trigger.
